Hi Aisha —

Thanks — this is a good heads-up. I put together three options and a short note on operational trade-offs. See attached (Greenline_Renewal_Options_v1.xlsx) — summary below. If any of these look promising I can follow up with a SOW and a DocuSign link.

Option A — 12 months, staged ramp + auto-renew (lowest upfront commit)
- Month 1–3: current baseline
- Month 4–6: +50% capacity
- Month 7–12: +150% capacity cap (burst available)
- Auto-renew yearly unless opt-out with 60-day notice
- Unit price: list price; single-year uplift of 8% for staged support

Option B — 36 months, stepped pricing (best unit economics)
- Year 1: baseline commit
- Year 2: +50% commit
- Year 3: +100% commit
- Annual price step-down: 7% in year 2, 12% in year 3 (on committed units)
- Co-terming allowed; finance prefers annual invoices or consolidated billing

Option C — Co-term only (align to Oct 1)
- Prorated billing to align terms; one-time co-terming admin fee (covers migration & invoice adjustments)

Notes:
- Co-terming requires proration of current invoice cycle; we can absorb up to 30 days of proration for no extra cost on Enterprise deals.
- For staged ramps, recommend prefix caching + burst pool for first 6 weeks to keep SLOs while caches warm.

I've CC'd Marissa for pricing flexibility and a quick internal green-light. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to run numbers with your procurement.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
